## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samuṭṭhānavāra* (Pvr 2.13) is a section of the *Parivāra*, the analytical concluding treatise of the Vinaya Piṭaka. Like many sections of the *Parivāra*, it is structured as a *vāra* (analytical division) compiled for practical monastic study and application [von Hinüber 1996]. In Vinaya terminology, *samuṭṭhāna* denotes the origination or causal mechanism of an offense [von Hinüber 1996]; this specific text defines monastic transgressions according to whether they originate in bodily action, vocal action, mental action, or combinations thereof. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 DharmaNexus does, however, record substantial Pali-internal text reuse comprising 199 matching passages across 21 texts, reflecting the standardized formulaic nature of Vinaya classification [DharmaNexus]. It shares extensive passages with other sections of the *Parivāra*, most notably the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1 and Pvr 1.9), the *Atthāpattisamuṭṭhāna* (Pvr 18), other *Samuṭṭhānavāra* sections (such as Pvr 1.5, Pvr 1.13, and Pvr 2.5), and various other *vāras* (Pvr 4, Pvr 2.14, Pvr 2.15, Pvr 2.16) [DharmaNexus]. Alignments also appear with later Vinaya literature, including the *Pācittiya-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Saṅgāyana-pucchā vissajjanā* [DharmaNexus].
